args.reason: The old decision rested on two stated assumptions: runs of under 20 issues and single-writer access. Both have stopped holding: runs now admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes issues in parallel. The new layout addresses the two named failures directly (lock contention on one file, and one corrupt write losing the whole run) and keeps the same directory root with an index file for discovery. Residual risk worth noting at build time: the index file and per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so the implementation needs a defined reconciliation rule. That is an implementation concern, not a flaw in the supersession argument.
